chunks: Thus, when the truth had come to them from Us, they said: 'Surely this is nothing but pure magic.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers call the truth 'clear magic' when it came to them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological barrier of *'urf* (customary expectation) and *kibr* (pride) that prevents recognition of truth even when accompanied by clear signs (*bayyinah*). The disbelievers' dismissal of divine revelation as 'clear magic' illustrates how entrenched dogma can distort perception, a theme central to the narrative of Musa (AS) in Surah Yunus and Al-A'raf. This rejection serves as a cautionary archetype for those who prioritize worldly authority over spiritual reality.
